p1.title: Intalim
p1.description: A fully automated education management system for driving schools: Face ID attendance tracking, online testing, video lessons, and electronic reporting in one platform.
p1.challenge: Over 1,000 driving schools across Uzbekistan tracked attendance on paper, students relied on scattered materials to prepare for exams, and directors and instructors had to compile reports manually in spreadsheets — costing time and introducing errors.
p1.solution: We combined Face ID biometric attendance (0.3-second recognition), an official exam bank of 1,250+ test questions, and animated video lessons into a single information system. Directors, moderators, accountants, instructors, and students each get a role-based panel, so every process is now tracked in real time.

p2.title: EAvtoTalim
p2.description: A unified information system for institutions that train, retrain, and upgrade the qualifications of motor vehicle drivers — the web version of the Intalim ecosystem.
p2.challenge: Driving license and qualification-upgrade schools needed more than a mobile app — a browser-based interface that could fully manage operations and digitize document workflows from a desktop.
p2.solution: We adapted Intalim's core features — student and instructor records, online testing, class schedules, attendance, and electronic reporting — into a fast, browser-based platform that syncs in real time with the Intalim mobile ecosystem, so data stays consistent no matter which device is used.

p3.title: Ustalar
p3.description: A broad marketplace connecting skilled workers with customers — plumbers, electricians, builders, and 50+ other specialties find jobs, while customers post orders quickly and reliably.
p3.challenge: Service professionals struggled to find a steady stream of customers and mostly relied on word of mouth, while customers had no reliable single place to find a vetted specialist or compare price and quality beforehand.
p3.solution: We built a two-sided marketplace: professionals create a profile listing their services, pricing, and past work, while customers describe their task and post an order or pick a specialist from the catalog. Verified professionals, a rating system, and secure payment infrastructure made the platform trustworthy — a locally adapted alternative to solutions like YouDo and Uzum Tezkor.

p4.title: Sales Auto.Bot
p4.description: A smart sales bot that talks with customers, takes orders, and automates payments.
p4.challenge: The customer support team was manually handling hundreds of repetitive requests every day.
p4.solution: Launched an OpenAI-powered Telegram bot with order intake and payment automation features.

p5.title: Corporate Suite
p5.description: A high-load corporate portal combining employee management, reporting, and internal communication in one system.
p5.challenge: The company operated across several disconnected systems (spreadsheets, email, legacy software).
p5.solution: A single corporate portal on PostgreSQL in Docker containers unified all workflows.

face-id-attendance-case-study.title: How We Built a Face ID Attendance System for Driving Schools
face-id-attendance-case-study.excerpt: A practical look at how we replaced paper attendance logs with a biometric system that recognizes a face in 0.3 seconds, from the Intalim project.
content: When we started working on Intalim, the biggest pain point for driving schools was obvious: attendance was tracked on paper, which meant errors, wasted time, and no real oversight. Instructors marked dozens of names by hand every lesson, and directors spent hours compiling monthly reports in spreadsheets.

The first decision was choosing the right authentication method. Fingerprint scanners needed extra hardware and raised hygiene concerns, so we went with camera-based Face ID — all it needs is a regular webcam or a smartphone.

The hardest technical challenge was delivering speed and accuracy at the same time. Dozens of students needed to check in within minutes at the start of class. Through an optimized model and efficient indexing, we reached a 0.3-second recognition time with 99.9% accuracy — a delay that's practically unnoticeable in a real classroom.

The second phase was making that data useful. Beyond just 'who showed up,' we linked attendance statistics, fee calculations, and exam readiness together. Directors now see real-time reporting across every branch from a single dashboard, and accountants get attendance-based billing calculated automatically.

The result: over 1,000 driving schools have fully moved off paper logs, report preparation dropped from hours to seconds, and students can check their attendance percentage anytime from their own account. This project confirmed for us that sophisticated technology — biometrics, real-time sync — solves everyday problems simply and fast when it's applied the right way.

eavtotalim-case-study.title: EAvtoTalim: From One Mobile App to a Unified Web Ecosystem
eavtotalim-case-study.excerpt: A practical look at how we built the web version of Intalim for institutions that train and license drivers.
content: After the Intalim mobile app launched successfully, we kept hearing the same request from driving school directors and instructors: "Can we manage this fully from a computer?" The mobile app worked great for students, but administrative work — document workflows, building class schedules, entering large batches of student data — really needed a bigger screen and a keyboard.

That's how EAvtoTalim came to be: a unified information system for institutions that train, retrain, and upgrade the qualifications of motor vehicle drivers, built as the web version of the Intalim ecosystem.

The biggest technical requirement was keeping data in real-time sync with the mobile app. If an instructor changed a class schedule in the web panel, that change needed to appear in the student's mobile app instantly. We solved this by connecting both platforms to a shared backend and REST API — one single source of truth, not two separate databases drifting apart.

The second key decision was simplifying the experience for each type of user. We built role-based panels for directors, accountants, and instructors: directors see statistics across every branch, accountants handle billing and penalties, and instructors only see their own group. This made a genuinely complex system feel simple and clear for each person using it.

Today, directors run their entire institution from any device — desktop, tablet, or phone — through EAvtoTalim. This project taught us something worth remembering: for a mobile-first product to truly succeed, its web counterpart sometimes needs just as much careful thought.

ustalar-marketplace-case-study.title: Ustalar: Building a Two-Sided Marketplace From Scratch
ustalar-marketplace-case-study.excerpt: A practical look at how we designed a marketplace connecting skilled workers with customers.
content: The idea behind Ustalar came from a simple observation: when people need a plumber, electrician, or builder, they usually turn to word of mouth or scroll through random ads on social media. There was no reliable single place to find a trusted professional, and professionals themselves had no steady stream of customers.

This is a classic two-sided marketplace problem: neither side can find the other because there's no trusted platform connecting them. We set out to solve it, drawing inspiration from international models like YouDo and Uzum Tezkor, but adapted to local market needs.

The most important architectural decision was building two completely different interfaces — for professionals and for customers — that share the same underlying data. A professional creates a profile listing their services, pricing, and photos of past work. A customer describes their task in a few sentences and either posts an order instantly or searches the catalog for the right match.

To build trust, we added three mechanisms: a verification process for professionals, a rating and review system from customers, and secure payment infrastructure. This lets a customer quickly answer "can I trust this person?", while giving professionals a clear incentive — better work means more orders.

Today, the Ustalar platform covers 50+ service categories with orders managed in real time. This project showed us the real secret to building a marketplace: it's not the technology — it's a trust mechanism that feels fair and transparent to both sides.

faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.description: Find answers to the key questions you should know before starting your project.

items.question: How long does a project take to complete?
items.answer: A simple landing page takes 1-2 weeks, while a complex web platform or mobile app takes 4-8 weeks. The exact timeline is set once the technical specification (TS) is ready.

items.question: How is the project price determined?
items.answer: Price depends on project complexity, functionality, and timeline. We provide a free consultation and an exact quote for every project.

items.question: Is there technical support after the project is done?
items.answer: Yes, every project includes 24/7 technical support and free bug fixes for an agreed period.

items.question: What technologies do you use?
items.answer: We mainly use Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Node.js. Depending on project requirements, we also use Python, PostgreSQL, and other modern technologies.

items.question: Can you upgrade my existing website?
items.answer: Absolutely. We'll analyze your current project and prepare a proposal for migrating to modern technology or extending its functionality.

items.question: How does payment work?
items.answer: Projects are usually split into 2-3 stages, with payment made at the completion of each stage. Upfront payment terms are agreed at the start of the project.

3.2. Project information. When you request a service, we may store project requirements, technical specifications, budget scope, and other materials shared during our discussions.
3.3. Technical information. When you visit the site, technical information (browser type, device type, IP address, page access times) may be automatically collected through analytics services.

Your information is never sold or rented to third parties for marketing or any other purposes.
